title: Section 118 — Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means

content.overview: BNS s. 118 — Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means (old 324/326). Weapons, fire, poison, explosive, acid-like substances. BNS restatement of IPC 324 / 326. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 118 is the rule on “Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means”. The section provides that (1) Whoever, except in the case provided for by sub-section (1) of section 122, voluntarily causes hurt by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting, or any instrument which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, or by means of fire or any heated substance, or by means of any poison or any corrosive substance, or by means of any explosive substance, or by means of any substance which it is deleterious to the human body to inhale, to swallow, or to receive into the blood, or by means of any animal, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 118 exists so that “Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

learningObjectives: Master the aggravated offences of causing hurt and grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means under BNS s. 118.
Analyze the enumerated weapons and dangerous instruments: shooting, stabbing, cutting, fire, corrosive substance, poison, explosive, or animal means.
Contrast sub-section (1) (hurt: up to 3 years and fine) with sub-section (2) (grievous hurt: life imprisonment or up to 10 years and fine).
Appreciate the consolidation of old IPC ss. 324 and 326.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 118 consolidates the offences of causing hurt and grievous hurt by dangerous weapons: sub-section (1) punishes voluntarily causing hurt by any instrument for shooting, stabbing, or cutting, or instrument used as a weapon of offence likely to cause death, or by fire, heated substance, poison, corrosive substance, explosive, or animal with imprisonment up to three years, fine, or both; sub-section (2) punishes voluntarily causing grievous hurt by any such dangerous weapons or means with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Imposes severe aggravated penalties when physical violence is executed using lethal instruments, fire, explosives, poisons, or animals capable of causing death.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 118 (consolidating IPC ss. 324 and 326).
Sub-section (1): Voluntarily causing simple hurt by dangerous weapons or means — imprisonment of either description up to three years, or fine, or both.
Sub-section (2): Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means — imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
Enumerated instruments: Instruments for shooting, stabbing, or cutting; weapons likely to cause death; fire or heated substances; poison or corrosive substances; explosives; animals.
Exception: Except in cases provided for by Section 122 (on provocation).
essentialIngredients: The accused voluntarily caused hurt (for sub-section 1) OR grievous hurt (for sub-section 2).
The hurt was caused by means of an instrument for shooting, stabbing, or cutting; OR
By an instrument used as a weapon of offence likely to cause death; OR
By fire, heated substance, poison, corrosive substance, explosive, or noxious inhaling substance; OR
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 118 consolidates former IPC 324 (hurt by dangerous weapons) and IPC 326 (grievous hurt by dangerous weapons) into a single cohesive section with two sub-sections. The aggravating factor is the dangerous character of the weapon or means employed. The section enumerates specific categories: cutting/stabbing weapons (knives, swords, daggers), shooting instruments (firearms), fire or heated substances (branding with irons, boiling water), chemicals and poisons (corrosives, toxic gases), explosives, and setting dangerous animals on someone. Under sub-section (1), if simple hurt is caused, the punishment extends up to three years. Under sub-section (2), if grievous hurt is caused, the offence becomes a grave felony punishable with imprisonment for life or up to ten years imprisonment and fine.
examples: Teaching example (Section 118(1) - Knife slash causing simple hurt): An accused slashes a victim's forearm with a hunting knife during a street fight, causing a five-centimeter laceration that requires stitches but involves no fracture or permanent impairment. The accused is liable under s. 118(1) (up to three years).

Teaching example (Section 118(2) - Sword blow causing fracture): An accused strikes a victim's arm with a sword, cutting through muscle and fracturing the ulna bone. The injury constitutes grievous hurt caused by a cutting weapon; the accused is liable under s. 118(2) (life imprisonment tier).
distinctions: Section 118(1) vs Section 115: Section 115 applies to simple hurt by ordinary means (up to 1 year); Section 118(1) applies when simple hurt is caused by dangerous weapons (up to 3 years).

Section 118(2) vs Section 124 (Acid attack): While s. 118(2) covers corrosive substances generally, Section 124 is a specialized provision for acid attacks carrying a mandatory minimum of 10 years to natural life.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who threw boiling oil on a shopkeeper's leg, causing deep third-degree burns and permanent disabling contraction of the knee joint, is liable under s. 118(2).
Rule: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by means of a heated substance constitutes an offence under BNS s. 118(2).
Application: Boiling oil is a heated substance and the resulting permanent joint impairment constitutes grievous hurt under s. 116(e).
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under BNS s. 118(2) and liable to imprisonment for life.
